title: Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 47-2314 — Implied warranty; merchantability
content:
Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 47-2314

A. Unless excluded or modified (§ 47-2316), a warranty that the goods shall be merchantable is implied in a contract for their sale if the seller is a merchant with respect to goods of that kind.

B. Goods to be merchantable must be at least such as:

1. Pass without objection in the trade under the contract description; and

3. Are fit for the ordinary purposes for which such goods are used.

sections.content: Arizona UCC implies a merchantability warranty when the seller is a merchant of goods of that kind.

title: Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1368 — Noncompliance with rental agreement by tenant
content:
Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1368

A. Except as provided in this chapter, if there is a material noncompliance by the tenant with the rental agreement or a noncompliance with § 33-1341 materially affecting health and safety, the landlord may deliver a written notice to the tenant specifying the acts and omissions constituting the breach and that the rental agreement will terminate upon a date not less than ten days after receipt of the notice if the breach is not remedied.

sections.content: Arizona landlords may terminate for material tenant noncompliance after written notice allowing at least ten days to cure.

title: Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 12-401 — Venue
content:
Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 12-401

No person shall be sued out of the county in which he resides, except:

1. When a civil action is commenced against a railroad company, it may be brought in any county through or into which the railroad runs.

14. When the foundation of the action is a crime, offense or trespass for which an action in damages may lie, the action may be brought in the county in which the crime, offense or trespass was committed or in the county in which the defendant or any of the several defendants reside.

sections.content: Arizona venue generally lies in the county of the defendant's residence, with statutory exceptions.

title: Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 12-2201 — Competency of witnesses
content:
Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 12-2201

A. Every person is competent to be a witness except as otherwise provided by statute or rule.

B. This section does not affect the competency of a witness under any other statute or rule of evidence.

sections.content: Arizona provides that every person is competent to be a witness except as otherwise provided by statute or rule.

title: Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 18-552 — Notification of security system breach
content:
Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 18-552

A. When a person that conducts business in this state and that owns or licenses unencrypted and unredacted computerized personal information becomes aware of a security system breach, that person shall conduct an investigation to promptly determine whether there has been a security system breach.

B. If the investigation determines that there has been a security system breach, the person shall notify the individuals affected.

sections.content: Arizona requires investigation and notification following a security system breach involving personal information.

title: Colo. Rev. Stat. § 4-2-314 — Implied warranty: merchantability
content:
Colo. Rev. Stat. § 4-2-314

(1) Unless excluded or modified (section 4-2-316), a warranty that the goods shall be merchantable is implied in a contract for their sale if the seller is a merchant with respect to goods of that kind.

(2) Goods to be merchantable must be at least such as:

(a) Pass without objection in the trade under the contract description; and

(c) Are fit for the ordinary purposes for which such goods are used.

sections.content: Colorado UCC implies merchantability when the seller is a merchant of goods of that kind.

title: Colo. Rev. Stat. § 13-40-104 — Forcible entry and detainer; when maintainable
content:
Colo. Rev. Stat. § 13-40-104

(1) A person is entitled to the remedy of forcible entry and detainer when:

(a) The person is entitled to the possession of lands, tenements, or other real property and an unlawful entry or detention has been made thereon;

(d) A tenant fails to pay rent when due and remains in possession after demand.

sections.content: Colorado FED remedy is available for unlawful detention including nonpayment of rent after demand.

title: Colo. Rev. Stat. § 13-1-124 — Jurisdiction of courts

sections.content: Colorado long-arm statute reaches nonresidents who transact business or commit tortious acts in the state.

title: Colo. Rev. Stat. § 13-25-127 — Competency of witnesses
content:
Colo. Rev. Stat. § 13-25-127

All persons, without exception, other than those specified in sections 13-90-101 to 13-90-108, may be witnesses. Neither parties nor other persons who have an interest in the event of an action or proceeding are excluded.

sections.content: Colorado generally treats all persons as competent witnesses except as otherwise provided by statute.

title: Colo. Rev. Stat. § 6-1-716 — Notification of security breach
content:
Colo. Rev. Stat. § 6-1-716

(2) A covered entity that maintains computerized data that includes personal identifying information shall, when it becomes aware of a breach of the security of the system, conduct in good faith a prompt investigation to determine the likelihood that personal identifying information has been or will be misused.

(3) If the investigation determines that misuse has occurred or is likely to occur, the covered entity shall give notice to affected Colorado residents.

sections.content: Colorado requires investigation and notice to residents after a security breach involving personal identifying information.

title: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 42a-2-314 — Implied warranty: merchantability
content:
Conn. Gen. Stat. § 42a-2-314

(1) Unless excluded or modified as provided in section 42a-2-316, a warranty that the goods shall be merchantable is implied in a contract for their sale if the seller is a merchant with respect to goods of that kind.

(2) Goods to be merchantable must be at least such as (a) pass without objection in the trade under the contract description; and (c) are fit for the ordinary purposes for which such goods are used.

sections.content: Connecticut UCC implies merchantability for merchant sellers of goods of that kind.

title: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-15 — Noncompliance by tenant
content:
Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-15

Prior to the commencement of a summary process action, except in the case where the landlord elects to proceed under sections 47a-23 to 47a-23b, inclusive, the landlord shall deliver a written notice to the tenant specifying the acts or omissions constituting the breach and that the rental agreement shall terminate upon a date not less than fifteen days after receipt of the notice if the breach is not remedied.

sections.content: Connecticut landlords must deliver written cure notice before most summary process actions for tenant breach.

title: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 52-59b — Jurisdiction over nonresident

sections.content: Connecticut long-arm jurisdiction reaches nonresidents who transact business or commit tortious acts in the state.

title: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 52-145 — Competency of witnesses
content:
Conn. Gen. Stat. § 52-145

No person shall be disqualified as a witness in any action by reason of interest in the event of the action as a party or otherwise, or by reason of the person's conviction of crime.

sections.content: Connecticut does not disqualify witnesses solely for interest in the action or conviction of crime.

title: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 36a-701b — Breach of security
content:
Conn. Gen. Stat. § 36a-701b

(b) Any person who conducts business in this state, and who, in the course of such business, owns, licenses or maintains computerized data that includes personal information, shall provide notice of any breach of security following discovery or notification of the breach to any resident of this state whose personal information was, or is reasonably believed to have been, accessed by an unauthorized person.

sections.content: Connecticut requires notice to residents after a security breach involving personal information.

title: Ga. Code Ann. § 11-2-314 — ucc_merchantability
content:
Ga. Code Ann. § 11-2-314

(1) Unless excluded or modified (Code Section 11-2-316), a warranty that the goods shall be merchantable is implied in a contract for their sale if the seller is a merchant with respect to goods of that kind.

sections.content: UCC merchantability warranty for merchant sellers.

title: Ga. Code Ann. § 44-7-50 — landlord_tenant
content:
Ga. Code Ann. § 44-7-50

(a) In all cases where a tenant holds possession of lands or tenements over and beyond the term for which they were rented or leased to him or fails to pay the rent when due, the landlord may demand possession.

sections.content: Demand for possession available for holdover or unpaid rent.

title: Ga. Code Ann. § 9-10-91 — personal_jurisdiction

sections.content: Georgia long-arm reaches nonresidents who transact business or commit torts in the state.

title: Ga. Code Ann. § 24-6-601 — evidence_relevance
content:
Ga. Code Ann. § 24-6-601

Every person is competent to be a witness except as otherwise provided in this chapter.

sections.content: Every person is competent to be a witness except as otherwise provided.

title: Ga. Code Ann. § 10-1-912 — data_breach
content:
Ga. Code Ann. § 10-1-912

(a) Any information broker or data collector that maintains computerized data that includes personal information of individuals shall give notice of any breach of the security of the system following discovery or notification of the breach in the security of the data to any resident of this state whose unencrypted personal information was, or is reasonably believed to have been, acquired by an unauthorized person.

sections.content: Georgia requires breach notice to residents whose personal information may have been acquired.

title: La. Civ. Code art. 2524 — implied_warranty
content:
La. Civ. Code art. 2524

The thing sold must be reasonably fit for its ordinary use.

When the seller has reason to know the particular use the buyer intends for the thing, or the buyer's particular purpose for the thing, and that the buyer is relying on the seller's skill or judgment, the thing sold must be fit for the buyer's intended use or for his particular purpose.

sections.content: Louisiana warranty of fitness for ordinary and particular use.

title: La. R.S. § 12:91 — director_duties
content:
La. R.S. § 12:91

A. Officers and directors shall be deemed to stand in a fiduciary relation to the corporation and its shareholders, and shall discharge the duties of their respective positions in good faith, and with that diligence, care, judgment and skill which ordinarily prudent men would exercise under similar circumstances in like positions.

sections.content: Louisiana directors and officers owe fiduciary duties of good faith and care.

title: La. Code Evid. art. 401 — evidence_relevance
content:
La. Code Evid. art. 401

"Relevant evidence" means evidence having any tendency to make the existence of any fact that is of consequence to the determination of the action more probable or less probable than it would be without the evidence.

sections.content: Louisiana defines relevant evidence by tendency to make a consequential fact more or less probable.

title: La. R.S. § 51:3074 — data_breach
content:
La. R.S. § 51:3074

A. Any person that conducts business in the state or that owns or licenses computerized data that includes personal information, or any agency that owns or licenses computerized data that includes personal information, shall, following discovery of a breach in the security of the system containing such data, notify any resident of the state whose personal information was, or is reasonably believed to have been, acquired by an unauthorized person.

sections.content: Louisiana requires breach notification to affected residents.

title: La. R.S. § 49:950 — administrative_procedure
content:
La. R.S. § 49:950

This Chapter may be cited as the Administrative Procedure Act.

sections.content: Louisiana Administrative Procedure Act citation provision.

title: Md. Code Ann., Com. Law § 2-314 — ucc_merchantability
content:
Md. Code Ann., Com. Law § 2-314

(1) Unless excluded or modified (§ 2-316), a warranty that the goods shall be merchantable is implied in a contract for their sale if the seller is a merchant with respect to goods of that kind.

sections.content: Maryland UCC merchantability warranty.

title: Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-402 — landlord_tenant
content:
Md. Code Ann., Real Prop. § 8-402

(a) A landlord may make complaint in writing to the District Court that a tenant holds over beyond the expiration of the lease, or that a tenant fails to pay rent.

sections.content: Maryland landlord may complain for holdover or unpaid rent.

normalizedCitation: Md. Code Ann., Cts. & Jud. Proc. § 6-103

Except as otherwise provided by law, every person is competent to be a witness.

sections.content: Maryland general witness competency.

title: Md. Code Ann., Com. Law § 14-3504 — data_breach
content:
Md. Code Ann., Com. Law § 14-3504

(b) A business that owns or licenses computerized data that includes personal information of an individual residing in the State shall conduct in good faith a reasonable and prompt investigation to determine the likelihood that personal information of the individual has been or will be misused as a result of the breach of security.

sections.content: Maryland requires investigation after a security breach involving personal information.

title: Mich. Comp. Laws § 445.903 — consumer_protection
content:
Mich. Comp. Laws § 445.903

(1) Unfair, unconscionable, or deceptive methods, acts, or practices in the conduct of trade or commerce are unlawful and are defined as follows:

(a) Causing a probability of confusion or misunderstanding as to the source, sponsorship, approval, or certification of goods or services.

sections.content: Michigan Consumer Protection Act unfair practices.

title: Mich. Comp. Laws § 554.139 — landlord_tenant
content:
Mich. Comp. Laws § 554.139

(1) In every lease or license of residential premises, the lessor or licensor covenants:

(a) That the premises and all common areas are fit for the use intended by the parties.

(b) To keep the premises in reasonable repair during the term of the lease or license.

sections.content: Michigan residential implied covenants of habitability and repair.

title: Mich. Comp. Laws § 600.705 — personal_jurisdiction
content:
Mich. Comp. Laws § 600.705

The existence of any of the following relationships between an individual or his agent and the state shall constitute a sufficient basis of jurisdiction to enable a court of record of this state to exercise limited personal jurisdiction over the individual and to enable the court to render personal judgments against the individual or his representative arising out of an act which creates any of the following relationships:

(1) The transaction of any business within the state.

(2) The doing or causing an act to be done, or causing the consequences of an act to occur, in the state resulting in an action for tort.

sections.content: Michigan limited personal jurisdiction bases.

title: Mich. Comp. Laws § 600.2159 — evidence_relevance
content:
Mich. Comp. Laws § 600.2159

No person shall be excluded from giving evidence in any action or proceeding by reason of crime or interest, except as otherwise provided by law.

sections.content: Michigan generally does not exclude witnesses for crime or interest.

title: Mich. Comp. Laws § 445.72 — data_breach
content:
Mich. Comp. Laws § 445.72

(1) Unless the person or agency determines that the security breach has not or is not likely to cause substantial loss or injury to, or result in identity theft with respect to, 1 or more residents of this state, a person or agency that owns or licenses data that are included in a database that discovers a security breach shall provide a notice of the security breach to each resident of this state who meets 1 or more of the following:

(a) That resident's unencrypted and unredacted personal information was accessed and acquired by an unauthorized person.

sections.content: Michigan security breach notice to residents.

title: N.C. Gen. Stat. § 75-1.1 — consumer_protection
content:
N.C. Gen. Stat. § 75-1.1

(a) Unfair methods of competition in or affecting commerce, and unfair or deceptive acts or practices in or affecting commerce, are declared unlawful.

sections.content: North Carolina UDTPA.

title: N.C. Gen. Stat. § 42-3 — landlord_tenant
content:
N.C. Gen. Stat. § 42-3

In all verbal or written leases of real property of any kind in which is fixed a definite time for the termination of the tenancy, there is implied a condition of forfeiture for nonpayment of the rent reserved.

sections.content: North Carolina implied forfeiture for nonpayment of rent.

title: N.C. Gen. Stat. § 1-75.4 — personal_jurisdiction
content:
N.C. Gen. Stat. § 1-75.4

A court of this State having jurisdiction of the subject matter has jurisdiction over a person served in an action pursuant to Rule 4(j), Rule 4(j1), or Rule 4(j3) of the Rules of Civil Procedure under any of the following circumstances:

(1) Local Presence or Status. — In any action, whether the claim arises within or without this State, in which a claim is asserted against a party who when service of process is made:

a. Is a natural person present within this State; or

(4) Local Injury; Foreign Act. — In any action claiming injury to person or property within this State arising out of an act or omission outside this State by the defendant.

sections.content: North Carolina personal jurisdiction statute.

title: N.C. Gen. Stat. § 8C-1, Rule 601 — evidence_relevance
content:
N.C. Gen. Stat. § 8C-1, Rule 601

Every person is competent to be a witness except as otherwise provided in these rules.

sections.content: North Carolina witness competency.

title: N.C. Gen. Stat. § 75-65 — data_breach
content:
N.C. Gen. Stat. § 75-65

(a) Any business that owns or licenses personal information of residents of North Carolina or any business that conducts business in North Carolina that owns or licenses personal information in any form (whether computerized, paper, or otherwise) shall provide notice to the affected person that there has been a security breach following discovery or notification of the breach.

sections.content: North Carolina security breach notification.

title: Ohio Rev. Code § 1345.02 — consumer_protection
content:
Ohio Rev. Code § 1345.02

(A) No supplier shall commit an unfair or deceptive act or practice in connection with a consumer transaction. Such an unfair or deceptive act or practice by a supplier violates this section whether it occurs before, during, or after the transaction.

sections.content: Ohio Consumer Sales Practices Act unfair or deceptive acts.

title: Ohio Rev. Code § 5321.04 — landlord_tenant

sections.content: Ohio landlord duties of habitability and repair.

title: Ohio Rev. Code § 2307.382 — personal_jurisdiction

sections.content: Ohio long-arm statute.

title: Ohio Rev. Code § 2317.01 — evidence_relevance
content:
Ohio Rev. Code § 2317.01

All persons are competent witnesses except those of unsound mind and children under ten years of age who appear incapable of receiving just impressions of the facts and transactions respecting which they are examined, or of relating them truly.

sections.content: Ohio general witness competency.

title: Ohio Rev. Code § 1349.19 — data_breach
content:
Ohio Rev. Code § 1349.19

(B) Any person that owns or licenses computerized data that includes personal information shall disclose any breach of the security of the system, following its discovery or notification of the breach of the security of the system, to any resident of this state whose personal information was, or reasonably is believed to have been, accessed and acquired by an unauthorized person if the access and acquisition by the unauthorized person causes or reasonably is believed will cause a material risk of identity theft or other fraud to the resident.

sections.content: Ohio security breach disclosure to residents.

title: Wash. Rev. Code § 62A.2-314 — ucc_merchantability
content:
Wash. Rev. Code § 62A.2-314

(1) Unless excluded or modified (RCW 62A.2-316), a warranty that the goods shall be merchantable is implied in a contract for their sale if the seller is a merchant with respect to goods of that kind.

sections.content: Washington UCC merchantability.

content:
Wash. Rev. Code § 59.18.130

Each tenant shall pay the rental amount at such times and in such amounts as provided for in the rental agreement or as otherwise provided by law and comply with all obligations imposed upon tenants by applicable provisions of all municipal, county, and state codes, statutes, ordinances, and regulations.

sections.content: Washington Residential Landlord-Tenant Act tenant obligations.

title: Wash. Rev. Code § 4.28.185 — personal_jurisdiction

sections.content: Washington long-arm statute.

title: Wash. Rev. Code § 5.60.020 — evidence_relevance
content:
Wash. Rev. Code § 5.60.020

Every person of sound mind and discretion, except as hereinafter provided, may be a witness in any action, or proceeding.

sections.content: Washington general witness competency.

title: Wash. Rev. Code § 19.255.010 — data_breach
content:
Wash. Rev. Code § 19.255.010

(1) Any person or business that conducts business in this state and that owns or licenses data that includes personal information shall disclose any breach of the security of the system following discovery or notification of the breach in the security of the data to any resident of this state whose personal information was, or is reasonably believed to have been, acquired by an unauthorized person and the personal information was not secured.

sections.content: Washington security breach disclosure.

title: Wis. Stat. § 402.314 — ucc_merchantability
content:
Wis. Stat. § 402.314

(1) Unless excluded or modified as provided in s. 402.316, a warranty that the goods shall be merchantable is implied in a contract for their sale if the seller is a merchant with respect to goods of that kind.

sections.content: Wisconsin UCC merchantability.

title: Wis. Stat. § 704.17 — landlord_tenant
content:
Wis. Stat. § 704.17

(2) If a tenant under a lease for one year or less, or a year-to-year tenant, fails to pay any installment of rent when due, the tenancy is terminated if the landlord gives the tenant notice requiring the tenant to pay rent or vacate on or before a date at least 5 days after the giving of the notice.

sections.content: Wisconsin rent default notice and termination.

title: Wis. Stat. § 801.05 — personal_jurisdiction
content:
Wis. Stat. § 801.05

A court of this state having jurisdiction of the subject matter has jurisdiction over a person served in an action pursuant to s. 801.11 under any of the following circumstances:

(1) Local presence or status. In any action whether arising within or without this state, against a defendant who when the action is commenced:

(a) Is a natural person present within this state when served; or

(3) Local act or omission. In any action claiming injury to person or property within or without this state arising out of an act or omission within this state by the defendant.

sections.content: Wisconsin personal jurisdiction statute.

title: Wis. Stat. § 906.01 — evidence_relevance
content:
Wis. Stat. § 906.01

Every person is competent to be a witness except as otherwise provided in these rules.

sections.content: Wisconsin witness competency.

title: Wis. Stat. § 134.98 — data_breach
content:
Wis. Stat. § 134.98

(2) If an entity whose principal place of business is located in this state or an entity that maintains personal information of a resident of this state knows that personal information in the entity's possession has been acquired by a person whom the entity has not authorized to acquire the personal information, the entity shall make reasonable efforts to notify each resident who is the subject of the personal information.

sections.content: Wisconsin personal information acquisition notice.

title: 10 Del. C. § 4301 — Competency of witnesses
content:
10 Del. C. § 4301

No person shall be excluded from giving evidence in any action or proceeding by reason of crime or interest, except as otherwise provided by law.

sections.content: Delaware general witness competency.

sections.content: Delaware security breach disclosure.

title: Fla. Stat. § 90.601 — General rule of competency
content:

sections.content: Florida general witness competency.

content:

(3) NOTICE TO INDIVIDUALS.—

sections.content: Florida breach notice to individuals.

title: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 233, § 20 — Competency of witnesses
content:

sections.content: Massachusetts witness competency.

title: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 93H, § 3 — Notice of breach of security
content:
Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 93H, § 3

content:
N.J. Stat. Ann. § 56:8-163

a. Any business that conducts business in New Jersey, or any public entity that compiles or maintains computerized records that include personal information, shall disclose any breach of security of those computerized records following discovery or notification of the breach to any customer who is a resident of New Jersey whose personal information was, or is reasonably believed to have been, accessed by an unauthorized person.

title: 42 Pa.C.S. § 5911 — Competency of witnesses generally

sections.content: Pennsylvania Breach of Personal Information Notification Act.

title: Tex. R. Evid. 601 — Competency to Testify in General
content:
Tex. R. Evid. 601

sections.content: Texas Rules of Evidence general competency.

content:

sections.content: Texas breach notification statute.

title: Va. Code Ann. § 8.01-396 — Competency of witnesses
content:
Va. Code Ann. § 8.01-396

No person shall be incompetent to testify because of interest, or because of being a party, or because of being the husband or wife of a party.

title: Va. Code Ann. § 18.2-186.6 — Breach of personal information notification
content:
Va. Code Ann. § 18.2-186.6

content:

sections.content: California APA chapter definitions for administrative adjudication.

title: La. R.S. § 51:1405 — Unfair acts or practices
content: La. R.S. § 51:1405\n\nA. Unfair methods of competition and unfair or deceptive acts or practices in the conduct of any trade or commerce are hereby declared unlawful.

sections.content: Louisiana Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law prohibits unfair or deceptive acts.

title: La. C.C. art. 3499 — Personal action; ten years
content: La. C.C. art. 3499\n\nUnless otherwise provided by legislation, a personal action is subject to a liberative prescription of ten years.

sections.content: Louisiana general personal-action liberative prescription is ten years unless otherwise provided.

title: Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.82 — Customer records; breach disclosure
content: Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.82\n\n(a) A person or business that conducts business in California, and that owns or licenses computerized data that includes personal information, shall disclose any breach of the security of the system following discovery or notification of the breach in the security of the data to any resident of California whose unencrypted personal information was, or is reasonably believed to have been, acquired by an unauthorized person.

sections.content: California requires disclosure of a security breach to affected California residents.
